one_line: A pull-request-like workspace for defining and approving AI delegation boundaries.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents propose, challenge, test, review, and approve explicit autonomy boundaries with revision history and guardrails.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central because the page holds live boundary, constraint, approval, and revision state that the agent must inspect and modify without self-approving.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a dedicated AI Delegation Boundary workflow with current authority, proposed changes, history, and human approval surfaces.
Packet describes Proposal → Challenge → Human Judgment → Re-test → Human Approval → Apply, with the agent unable to approve its own revision.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent, intentionally designed governance product and the packet describes a complete core workflow, though end-to-end behavior is not fully legible from the contact sheets.
execution_evidence: Video frames show consistent branded screens and multiple delegation-review states.
About text specifies guardrails, regression tests, revision history, and explicit apply semantics.
impact_rationale: Agent authority and human control are a real, growing problem; this offers a concrete review and audit model for teams deploying autonomous workflows.
impact_evidence: Product explicitly addresses where agent authority ends and human authority begins.
Frames present persistent approval and decision-memory concepts rather than generic chat.
creativity_rationale: The pull request metaphor for agent autonomy, including challenge and regression-test loops, is a memorable and unusually deep interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Hero framing says agents can act while authority needs a memory.
The product turns delegation itself into an inspectable, revisable collaborative artifact.
usability_note: Structured stages and visible approval state suggest strong usability for governance work, though the dense policy workflow may require onboarding.
standouts: Delegation boundary as a pull request
Agent cannot approve its own revision
advance_reason: High-leverage, high-originality governance workflow with substantial product evidence.

one_line: A browser extension that gates WebMCP writes behind explicit human consent.
what_it_does: Intercepts WebMCP tool registration and network writes, queues non-read-only calls, shows arguments and origin, and supports revocable per-site/tool allow rules.
leverage_rationale: The extension adds a general consent and network-enforcement layer to existing WebMCP sites, including sites with no integration changes; this is materially safer and more precise than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes document_start MAIN-world wrapping of registerTool and network-level detection of read-only tools issuing POSTs.
Frames show a browser/gallery workflow with terminal activity, status notifications, and a final approval form/dialog.
execution_rationale: The implementation description is technically specific and the video shows a coherent extension workflow, although small frames do not expose all approval details.
execution_evidence: Frames show repeated browser states, automation logs, notifications, and a final confirmation UI.
About text details MV3 service worker, MessagePort bridge, storage durability, and explicit decline behavior.
impact_rationale: Human authorization for agent write actions is a concrete safety need with broad applicability across WebMCP sites.
impact_evidence: Product gates writes while allowing reads freely and surfaces real tool arguments and site.
Packet explicitly handles deceptive readOnly annotations and revocable allow lists.
creativity_rationale: Applying transparent, origin/tool-scoped consent and network enforcement to WebMCP is a strong and practical security interaction model.
creativity_evidence: No-site-installation extension model works across unaware WebMCP sites.
Poisoned read-only behavior is caught at the network layer rather than inferred from text.
usability_note: The approval card and explicit decline semantics are user-centered; repeated approval could still create friction.
standouts: Arguments and origin visible in consent card
advance_reason: Strong practical safety layer with credible implementation detail and visible workflow evidence.

one_line: A source-grounded research mentor embedded beside a real paper.
what_it_does: Keeps a PDF, selected source anchors, explanations, annotations, claims, and knowledge graph connected while an agent helps users understand and organize research.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes active PDF identity, selected words, geometry, identifiers, and graph revision so the agent can act on exact source context rather than approximate page text.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a three-column paper reader with highlighted passages, mentor panel, and knowledge graph.
About text emphasizes immutable source anchors, active selection context, and source-linked actions.
execution_rationale: The video shows a polished, coherent reading workspace with paper viewer, mentor, highlights, and graph states; the stated workflow is unusually complete for its scope.
execution_evidence: Frames show onboarding, the Attention Is All You Need paper, highlighted text, mentor controls, and graph visualization.
Packet specifies seven response sections and claim labels distinguishing evidence, interpretation, background, and uncertainty.
impact_rationale: Undergraduate and research readers have a clear problem—understanding difficult papers without losing provenance—and the product directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Source-linked explanations remain adjacent to the original document.
Knowledge graph, annotations, and evidence trail preserve inspectability and undoability.
creativity_rationale: The persistent paper-centered workspace and claim-level provenance are a thoughtful synthesis beyond a generic research chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Product tagline and UI keep proof beside explanation.
Separate unreviewed semantic suggestions and labeled claim types show depth of concept.
usability_note: Three-column layout, highlighting, and persistent graph/annotation context make the workflow legible, though dense for novice readers.
standouts: Paper, mentor, and graph in one workspace
advance_reason: Exceptional evidence-backed research workflow with strong WebMCP leverage and impact.

one_line: A local study workspace where agents turn sources into linked notes and practice.
what_it_does: Collects PDFs, text, images, and pasted sources into Markdown study sheets with citations, linked ideas, diagrams, and generated practice questions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to local source and workspace state, enabling repeatable creation and editing of linked study artifacts beyond fragile UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Frames show an initially empty workspace becoming populated with agent-created pages and a formatted lesson.
About text says sources and workspace data stay in IndexedDB and tools read sources, edit content, link citations, and generate questions.
execution_rationale: The frames show a visible state transition from empty space to multiple pages and a formatted lesson, supporting a coherent core workflow.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows agent activity alongside populated document entries and selected document content.
A visible result is titled Lesson 1 – Memory Systems for AI Agents and includes structured text/table content.
impact_rationale: Source provenance and active practice are valuable to students and self-directed learners working across many documents.
impact_evidence: Product addresses losing track of which source supports each idea.
Study and Practice modes connect notes to question generation.
creativity_rationale: The shared document-centered human-agent study model is a fresh synthesis, though the underlying note and quiz categories are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent and learner jointly build linked paragraphs, callouts, diagrams, and practice material.
Local-first IndexedDB workspace reinforces the shared-state concept.
usability_note: The populated workspace and document preview are understandable; the breadth of content types may require organization affordances.
advance_reason: Credible agent-mediated study workflow with visible before/after evidence and clear audience value.

one_line: An AI career command center for job matching, applications, experiments, and interview practice.
what_it_does: Combines job search, document parsing and tailoring, resume A/B tracking, skill-gap recommendations, and voice mock interviews.
leverage_rationale: The packet claims broad AI career capabilities, but the video frames show only a marketing landing page and no demonstrated WebMCP or agent operation; general-purpose automation appears comparably capable.
leverage_evidence: Frames show hero, feature cards, workflow sections, and calls to action, not a tool trace or live product operation.
About text claims autonomous matching and A/B attribution but provides no frame evidence of WebMCP changing the workflow.
execution_rationale: The landing page is coherent and polished, but the central product workflow and claimed outputs are not demonstrated in the available evidence.
execution_evidence: Frames consistently show a dark career-platform marketing page.
No completed job application, generated resume, analyzed posting, or interview result is visible.
impact_rationale: Job seekers are a clear audience with real pain around fragmented search, tailoring, and interview preparation, but demonstrated fit is limited.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies job-search fragmentation and lack of feedback as the target problem.
Product claims matching, tailoring, A/B testing, and role-specific coaching.
creativity_rationale: The unified career command center and empirical resume testing add an angle to a crowded category, but the concept is not highly novel from the evidence.
creativity_evidence: Frames emphasize two interfaces, feature breadth, and a unified platform.
A/B callback attribution is a more distinctive element than generic job-search assistance.
usability_note: Marketing structure is clear, but the actual operational UX cannot be judged from the landing-page frames.
red_flags: Video evidence is packaging/marketing rather than a product run.
Many high-performance claims are not visibly substantiated.
advance_reason: Clear audience and polished presentation, but insufficient execution and WebMCP evidence for advancement.

one_line: A policy-enforced expense console where agents triage work but servers authorize money actions.
what_it_does: Uses role-scoped WebMCP tools and server policy to triage 40 expenses, detect poisoned memos and duplicates, and route approvals safely.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared state, role-scoped tools, deterministic server authorization, and one-call batch triage create a materially different and safer agent-money workflow than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes one authenticated session, analyst/manager tool surfaces, server-side policy, and structured refusal to human review.
Video frames show a cinematic governance narrative centered on authority and poisoned records; authoritative packet facts establish the product demo context.
execution_rationale: The stated scope is tightly focused and technically intentional, with explicit policy cases and safe escalation; frame evidence is more promotional than dashboard-legible.
execution_evidence: About text specifies 40 seeded expenses, caps, receipts, duplicate detection, role limits, and live board updates.
Video evidence visibly communicates throughput, authority, and poisoned-record concerns, though not detailed UI state.
impact_rationale: Finance teams need safe, auditable automation of approval queues; the product directly addresses authority, untrusted records, and human escalation.
impact_evidence: Server, not model, evaluates and authorizes money actions.
Poisoned memo and over-limit human review are concrete risk scenarios with explicit handling.
creativity_rationale: The combination of batch agent throughput, least privilege, server authorization, and prompt-injection-resistant record handling is a strong, memorable governance design.
creativity_evidence: Three visible beats are throughput, least privilege, and safe escalation.
Untrusted expense memo is deliberately kept outside policy evaluation.
usability_note: A single triage request and live board are strong operator affordances; role changes and exceptions may need careful explanation.
red_flags: Available frame sheet is highly cinematic and does not make the operational dashboard legible.
advance_reason: One of the strongest WebMCP governance concepts, with detailed safety semantics despite limited readable frame UI.

one_line: An agent-ready operations workspace for coordinating research protocols and study tasks.
what_it_does: Organizes studies, subjects, visits, assessments, samples, checklists, completion criteria, and advancement blockers in a shared workflow.
leverage_rationale: Protocol state is structured and cross-linked; WebMCP can inspect and synchronize operational records more reliably than inferring status from documents and pixels.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a multi-study operations dashboard, studies view, metrics, queue, and embedded contextual assistant.
Packet says fourteen imperative tools cover portfolio and protocol operations, including readiness and synchronized records.
execution_rationale: The dashboard and studies surfaces look coherent and intentionally scoped; the exact agent completion flow is only partially shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show Today’s study operations, summary metrics, work queue, Studies view, and agent panel.
About text enumerates workflow publishing, checklist generation, synchronized completion, and explicit advancement blockers.
impact_rationale: Research coordinators have a concrete coordination problem across protocols, subjects, visits, and assessments; a single operational source of truth has credible value.
impact_evidence: Product targets reconciliation across documents, spreadsheets, calendars, and task systems.
Synthetic study records and explicit no-PHI disclosure support a safe demo scope.
creativity_rationale: Turning a static research protocol into an agent-readable operational workflow is a strong synthesis, though adjacent workflow products exist.
creativity_evidence: Agent-ready study operations and context-to-next-action panel are integrated into the dashboard.
Readiness blockers and synchronized related records deepen the workflow model.
usability_note: Portfolio metrics and a focused assistant entry point support coordinators, though clinical workflow complexity is inherently high.
red_flags: Frame sheets show the assistant entry point more clearly than a completed agent operation.
advance_reason: Strong operational concept with clear structured-state WebMCP rationale and substantial dashboard evidence.

one_line: An agent-assisted racing-line editor that creates and stores track layouts on satellite maps.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect tracks and guidance, create or edit racing-line points, undo, save, load, and export browser-local lines with a 3D view.
leverage_rationale: Structured track context and point editing make agent generation precise and repeatable; a general UI agent would struggle with ordered geometry and drivable-surface constraints.
leverage_evidence: Frames show satellite circuit map, green racing line, WebMCP/JSON controls, local lines list, and a working agent panel.
About text explains point order, drivable surface, shared editor state, undo, save/load, and export.
execution_rationale: The video visibly demonstrates a coherent editor, generated line, browser-local storage, and export/delete controls, with a clear end-to-end result.
execution_evidence: Green racing line is visibly drawn over the circuit.
Browser-local lines list shows saved examples and export/delete actions.
Frames show an agent request and Working state over the map.
impact_rationale: Karting and track-learning users have a real niche need for preparing and studying unfamiliar circuits; the tool directly assists that task.
impact_evidence: Product supports braking, apex, acceleration, and transition points on satellite tracks.
Packet describes use for karting preparation and learning unfamiliar tracks.
creativity_rationale: Using an agent to construct meaningful ordered racing geometry on a map is distinctive and memorable, with the 3D/editor context supporting the idea deeply.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language agent generation of missing circuit layouts.
The product makes geometric constraints and visible edits part of the collaboration.
usability_note: Visible map result and local save/export controls make outcomes inspectable; racing-line correctness still requires domain expertise.
red_flags: The underlying editor predates the challenge, though the submission says it was separated and rebuilt as a standalone app.
standouts: Visible map result with local persistence
advance_reason: Excellent end-to-end evidence and a compelling case where structured tools outperform generic UI automation.

one_line: A live design canvas where agents can inspect, flag, and directly fix layout issues.
what_it_does: Exposes canvas state and element-level tools for flagging issues, moving/resizing elements, suggesting spacing, and placing exact annotations.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets an agent manipulate precise visual elements in shared canvas state, turning critique into directly observable edits rather than textual advice.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a landing/product workspace and lower execution/demo section built around agent hands and live execution.
About text lists getCanvasState, flagIssue, moveElement, resizeElement, suggestSpacing, and annotateAt.
execution_rationale: The concept and interface are coherent, but the supplied frame sheet is mostly promotional/product-tour imagery and does not clearly show a complete fix cycle.
execution_evidence: Frames show consistent product presentation, feature cards, and an execution area.
Packet describes a canvas toolbox and repeated agent-user back-and-forth on the same canvas.
impact_rationale: Designers and reviewers have a real communication gap when feedback is spatial; direct, exact manipulation can materially reduce iteration friction.
impact_evidence: Product addresses the mismatch between verbal design critique and visual fixes.
Agent can place issue badges and annotations on exact elements/positions.
creativity_rationale: Giving a design-review agent hands to touch the canvas is a fresh interaction model with a clear conceptual payoff.
creativity_evidence: Frames headline the transition from words to hands.
Element-level critique and correction are unified in one collaborative surface.
usability_note: Direct visible edits and badges should be understandable; users need undo/history safeguards for agent changes.
red_flags: Frame contact sheet does not clearly show an actual element being moved or resized.
standouts: Agent edits same canvas rather than only describing fixes
advance_reason: Strong interaction concept and credible tool surface, with moderate evidence limitations.

one_line: A workflow that turns business automation ideas into ROI, readiness, and implementation plans.
what_it_does: Runs deterministic diagnostics, hands results to opportunity and architecture specialists, and produces a bounded plan with human approval points and recalculated ROI.
leverage_rationale: Structured handoff between diagnostics and specialists is useful shared state, but the demonstrated business-case workflow could largely be achieved through a conventional agent or form-driven app.
leverage_evidence: Frames show an opportunity input area and a business-case output panel with a positive-looking recommendation and metrics.
About text describes five diagnostics, two specialist handoffs, deterministic Python calculations, and local Qwen interpretation.
execution_rationale: The frames show a polished, coherent input-to-output business-case interface, and the packet separates deterministic financial logic from model interpretation.
execution_evidence: Repeated frames visibly show the business opportunity evaluation surface and structured output.
Packet specifies ROI, operating cost, readiness diagnostics, implementation phases, and approval points.
impact_rationale: Businesses need help deciding which automation opportunities are viable and how to implement them, though the synthetic bounded demo limits proof of broader value.
impact_evidence: Product addresses opportunity selection, data readiness, operating costs, and implementation planning.
Output visibly includes a proceed-style recommendation and quantitative metrics.
creativity_rationale: The chained analyst-to-architect workflow and deterministic/model boundary are a thoughtful synthesis, though business-case planning is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Two complementary specialists receive a structured handoff.
Human approval points and recalculated ROI keep the plan bounded.
usability_note: A single evaluation-to-plan flow is approachable; users may need transparency into assumptions behind recommendations.
red_flags: Frame sheet repeats near-identical screens, limiting evidence of interaction progression.
Synthetic scenarios and local model constrain validation of real-world usefulness.
standouts: Deterministic financial calculations separated from model interpretation
advance_reason: Coherent and useful decision workflow with visible output, though WebMCP distinctiveness is moderate.
